liam: curry. yes. i'm in before you even ask

constraints_found.constraint: Quick lunch: must be fast, no long sit-down (Maya back by 1:00)
source_lines: maya: also my manager does a head count at 1:00 sharp. i cannot be the one strolling back in at 1:20
liam: so no long sit-down lunch. in, eat, out. my stomach and i are ready

maya: badly. my iced tea this morning cost what a whole lunch should. downtown is robbing me

source_lines: liam: ok ok. but mina orders a real main this time. no plate of fries

maya: oh, like pizza day when she offered to pick the pepperoni off. absolutely not
mina: ...okay. somewhere with a few curries i can actually order would be really nice. thank you both

venue_evaluation.downtown_tamarind_lane: curry, $, fast counter service, three vegetarian curries as full plates. Meets everything: 3 stars.
venue_evaluation.downtown_copper_pot: curry, $, fast, but every pot is meat; vegetarian only gets plain rice. Deal-breaker for Mina.
venue_evaluation.downtown_cardamom_house: curry, fast, vegetarian options, but $$ ('treat-yourself', stipend felt it). One tier over: 2 stars.
venue_evaluation.downtown_indigo_arch: curry, $, many vegetarian dishes, but slow coursed service made the reviewer late back to the office. Missed quick-lunch preference: 2 stars.
venue_evaluation.downtown_pepper_tree: burgers, $, fast, good veggie patty, but not curry. Missed craving: 2 stars.

notes: Vegetarian constraint is never stated outright; it must be inferred from the fries and pepperoni callbacks plus Mina's 'curries i can actually order'. Fair and well-signposted once you connect them, and every venue review uses 'doesn't eat meat' phrasing, which confirms the reading.
Liam's night-market noodle stall line is a red herring; Maya shuts it down immediately and no noodle venue is offered, so it is harmless.
Budget is never given as a tier; '$' is inferred from 'if it's pricey' and the iced-tea complaint. Cardamom House's '$$' plus 'treat-yourself' review makes the one-tier-over penalty clear.
Each distractor fails exactly one constraint, which is a clean design. Slightly easy once the vegetarian inference is made, since only one venue passes all four checks.

Uncertain whether the game treats inferred vegetarianism as a deal-breaker (strict diet) or a one-star preference; either way Tamarind Lane is the only 3-star pick, so the answer does not depend on it.
